messages:
Alex (Acme): hey team, running into a weird issue with the embeddings endpoint. When we send batched requests we sometimes get back vectors with the wrong dimension and occasional huge tail latencies. This started after we enabled dynamic batching on our Dedicated pool. Example error from our app: \"dimension mismatch: expected 1536, got 768\". Any ideas?
Maya (Support): sorry you're hitting this, can you paste a minimal repro (curl or SDK) and the model name/version you're calling? also which SDK version and whether you hit hosted or dedicated?
Alex (Acme): Hosted for now, model: redwood-embed-1 (we also have a rollout that includes redwood-embed-1-quant). SDK v0.9.2. Here's a shortened curl we use (we batch 8 inputs):
```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer $KEY\" \
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \
  -d '{\"model\":\"redwood-embed-1\",\"input\":[\"text1\",\"text2\",\"text3\",\"text4\",\"text5\",\"text6\",\"text7\",\"text8\"]}'
```
Alex (Acme): sample app log around the error: 
``
2026-03-14T18:32:10Z batch_id=xyz batch_size=8 route=embed-pool take=210ms first_tok=15 tail=190ms error=dimension_mismatch expected=1536 got=768
```
Maya (Support): thanks. two quick checks: 1) can you confirm if you pin model_version in the request body or rely on alias? 2) can you share pool config (max_batch_size / dynamic batching flags)?
Alex (Acme): we rely on alias (redwood-embed-1 -> rolling rollout that includes the quant variant). pool config from console: 
```json
{
  "pool": "embed-pool",
  "max_batch_size": 16,
  "dynamic_batching": true,
  "max_batch_bytes": 524288
}
```
Alex (Acme): when we set max_batch_size lower (we tried 4) latency spikes reduced but error still happened once.
Maya (Support): hm — two likely culprits: 1) dynamic batching may be packing requests targeted at different model variants (fp/quant) into the same batch if routing allows multiple variants in the pool, causing dimension mismatch. 2) if padding/truncation logic or pre-tokenization changed between variants you can get unexpected dims. I'm escalating to eng-ml + eng-runtime and sending your logs. Ticket #INC-2026-847. @Priya @Tom can you take a look?
deploy-bot: Automated note: related rollout redwood-embed-1-quant started 2026-03-14T16:00:00Z and targeted 20% of traffic.
Priya (Eng-ML): thanks @Maya, looking. my suspicion: quant variant emits 768-dim by mistake because of a model-variant mismatch (maybe someone registered a different architecture under the same alias). Can you confirm the registered dims for both variants? also, do you have the request-level model_version field from a failing call?
Alex (Acme): I can pull a failing request's headers/body. model_version header in one failing request: \"redwood-embed-1@v2026-03-10\". Console lists two variants: redwood-embed-1@v2026-03-08 (fp16, dim=1536) and redwood-embed-1@v2026-03-10 (quant, dim=1536) — both show 1536 in registry. but the kernel logs show 768 in the worker that processed the batch.
Tom (Eng-Runtime): adding runtime context: dynamic batching will coalesce requests up to max_batch_size and pack into a single kernel invocation. If a worker in the pool has a different model binary (mismatch on disk) or an old artifact, the returned tensor shape can differ. First step: can you reproduce by forcing traffic to the same pool but setting max_batch_size=1? that avoids coalescing. Also capture worker_id from logs so we can map to host.
Alex (Acme): reproduced with max_batch_size=1 — no dimension errors in 200 requests. Re-enabled max_batch_size=8 and error reappeared after ~120 requests. Worker id from failing log: worker-42.
Priya (Eng-ML): that strongly suggests an inconsistent artifact on worker-42. Tom / infra: can you check worker-42's model files and whether a half-quant build accidentally compiled to a 768-dim embedding (maybe a wrong checkpoint)? Also we should add a runtime validation that rejects batches when dims differ between inputs/models instead of silently returning suboptimal tensors.
Tom (Eng-Runtime): logged: assigning to eng-runtime oncall to pull worker-42 filesystem + kernel logs. quick mitigation: set pool to pin to one model_version (do not allow >1 variant in same pool) or temporarily disable dynamic_batching until we confirm artifacts. We'll also roll the fleet for that pool.
Maya (Support): forwarded repro payload and worker logs to eng teams, included the sample failing request, stack traces, and the batch trace from the runtime. Customers on the forum reported similar tail spikes; linking community thread.
Alex (Acme): we tried pinning the alias to v2026-03-08 and disabled dynamic batching for 30m — errors stopped and tail latencies dropped from 200ms to ~35ms at p95. Good temporary fix but would like to enable batching for cost reasons.
Priya (Eng-ML): next steps from ML side: audit model registry artifacts for both variants, confirm embedding head dims at export time, and add a CI check that verifies exported dims. We'll also add a model-metadata header so runtime can pre-check compatibility before packing.
Tom (Eng-Runtime): next steps from runtime: (1) add fast pre-batch compatibility check (compare model dims/metadata) before coalescing, (2) ensure worker agent validates model artifacts on startup and reports mismatch, (3) schedule a rolling redeploy of embed-pool to replace any bad artifacts. ETA: roll + tests ~48 hours.
Jenna (Support Manager): thanks everyone. summary for the customer: root cause likely inconsistent model artifact on a worker causing mismatched output dims when dynamic batching coalesced heterogeneous workers. mitigation: pin model_version or disable dynamic batching; temporary roll scheduled. I'll follow up once the eng teams complete the rollback/redeploy. 
Maya (Support): Alex — reopening this thread when we have production confirmation. for now we've applied the pin and lowered max_batch_size to 4 for your Dedicated pool. Please let us know if you see any more dimension errors. :thumbsup:
Alex (Acme): thanks all — that fixed it for now. appreciate the quick triage.
Tom (Eng-Runtime): assigned internal bug RINF-3214, adding owners Priya+Tom, linking logs and the failing request. will update here when rolled.
Priya (Eng-ML): added unit test to registry CI to assert embedding dims and model signature. PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/registry/pull/412
Maya (Support): closing loop for now, will post update when rollback complete.
